intro.title: Type a todo CRUD app with strict models
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple todo list application where you can create, read, update, and delete tasks. You will learn how to use TypeScript's type system to define strict models for your todo data, ensuring each task has a consistent structure. The main technologies involved are TypeScript interfaces and types to enforce these models. By the end, you'll understand how strong typing helps prevent errors and makes your code more predictable and maintainable.
intro.usecase: This pattern is essential for building any interactive data management interface, such as admin dashboards, customer relationship management (CRM) systems, or project management tools like Trello or Asana. For example, in a project management app, you need strict models to create, read, update, and delete tasks, ensuring data consistency across views like task lists, detail panels, and modal forms. As a developer, implementing typed CRUD operations prevents runtime errors, improves code maintainability, and provides clear interfaces for team collaboration, directly mirroring real-world scenarios where user data must be handled reliably and predictably.
